title: Ramesh Gupta v. Suresh Sharma
text: The complainant, Suresh Sharma, filed a complaint under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act against the drawer, Ramesh Gupta, for dishonour of a cheque of Rs 5,00,000. The cheque was returned by the bank with the endorsement 'Insufficient Funds'. The court examined the statutory demand notice sent by the complainant and found it to be legally valid. The drawer failed to repay the cheque amount within 15 days of receiving the notice. Under Section 138 NI Act, the dishonour of a cheque drawn for discharge of a legally enforceable debt gives rise to criminal liability. The court held that the ingredients of the offence are fully established. The complainant's evidence went unrebutted. The drawer's defence that the cheque was issued as security was rejected as it was not supported by any contemporaneous document. The drawer is held guilty under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act and sentenced to pay a fine of Rs 10,00,000 with simple imprisonment of one year in default. The complainant is awarded the cheque amount as compensation under Section 357 CrPC.
